CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Women are persons of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

BAB V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Pasal 25

The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII

PARTICIPATION

Article 33

1. Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, the business sector and other related stakeholders.

Pasal 28

1. Regional Government in an effort to provide and implement protection service handling for women victims of violence, exploitation and acts of violence shall establish UPTD PPA.
2. UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be under and responsible to the head of Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.

Integrated Services are the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women's and children's protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women's and children's protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

Article 22

The relevant agencies referred to are agencies that have a role in the implementation of women's empowerment in the social field, which may include women and children protection institutions, legal aid organizations and assistance for victims of violence, safe houses (shelters) that handle victims of gender-based violence, psychology practitioners and counselors, universities/educational institutions, community organizations, Family Welfare Empowerment, gender study centers at universities, family counseling consultation institutions, religious organizations that have women's empowerment programs, social rehabilitation centers.

CHAPTER III

EFFORTS FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

General

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Article 2

Letter a
What is meant by respect for human rights is respect, upholding the inherent human rights of citizens, and protecting dignity and honor as human beings.

Letter b
What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or action toward vulnerable groups of women with the aim that they obtain equal rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c
What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes an equal, harmonious and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in accessing, participating, controlling and benefiting in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d
What is meant by benefit is the implementation of protection for women that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Part Three

Services for Victims of Violence, Exploitation, and Discrimination

Pasal 26

Regional Government is responsible for:
a. implementing policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in order to realize the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women; and
c. applying service standards for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, the business sector and other related stakeholders.
3. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women; and
c. conducting skills training.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Letter b
What is meant by non-discrimination is protection for all women without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, belief, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, political choice, legal status and physical or mental condition. Special treatment or action toward vulnerable groups of women with the aim that they obtain equal rights is not included as an act of discrimination.

Letter c
What is meant by gender justice is fair treatment given to both women and men.

What is meant by gender equality is a condition and position that describes an equal, harmonious and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in accessing, participating, controlling and benefiting in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in society, nationhood and statehood.

Letter d
What is meant by benefit is the implementation of protection for women that provides benefits to women in the form of welfare, equality and justice, security and avoidance of all forms of violence, exploitation and discrimination.

Integrated Services are the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Article 1

Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Pasal 25

The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Women are persons of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

3. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

The implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of employment as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 5 shall be carried out by Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of labor and related agencies in the form of:
a. provision of skills and job training;
b. women have equal opportunities without discrimination to obtain employment; and
c. employers who employ female workers, provide access and skills training.

BAB V

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF REGIONAL GOVERNMENT

Pasal 25

The obligations of Regional Government in the implementation of protection and empowerment of women are as follows:
a. ensure the implementation of fulfillment of women's rights and provision of security guarantees from acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women in the Region;
b. establish policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women as well as guarantees for handling victims to eliminate all forms of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women in the Region; and
c. provide guidance and supervision in efforts to implement protection and empowerment of women carried out by Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment.

CHAPTER VIII

PARTICIPATION

Article 33

1. Every person and/or legal entity may participate in the implementation of the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.
2. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by individuals, groups or community social organizations, non-governmental organizations, educational institutions, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, religious institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, the business sector and other related stakeholders.
3. Participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may take the form of:
a. providing information or reporting to the competent authority if aware of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women;
b. taking preventive action against violence against women; and
c. conducting skills training.

Pasal 26

Regional Government is responsible for:
a. implementing policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in order to realize the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women; and
c. applying service standards for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 14

1. The implementation of family quality improvement aims to:
a. integrate policies, programs, and development activities whose targets are aimed at improving family quality;
b. strengthen and develop institutions providing family quality improvement services; and
c. provide standardized family quality improvement services.
2. Provisions regarding family quality improvement shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Bagian Kedua

UPTD PPA

Pasal 28

1. Regional Government in an effort to provide and implement protection service handling for women victims of violence, exploitation and acts of violence shall establish UPTD PPA.
2. UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be under and responsible to the head of Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection.
3. Further provisions regarding the establishment, main duties and functions as well as management of UPTD PPA as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Women are persons of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

Integrated Services are the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women's and children's protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women's and children's protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

Article 17

1. The implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of education as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 2 is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of education in the form of organizing formal and non-formal education.
2. Non-formal education as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to improve the capacity of women.

Article 18

The implementation of women's empowerment in the economic field as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 3 is carried out by the Regional Apparatus that administers governmental affairs in the field of micro, small and medium enterprises and related agencies in the form of:
a. facilitation of the formation and strengthening of productive economic business groups; and
b. facilitation of the development of marketing networks.

Article 20

What is meant by related agencies are agencies that have a role in the implementation of women's empowerment in the field of employment including Regional Apparatus that administer government affairs in the field of employment, Job Training Centers, cooperatives and micro, small and medium enterprises, State-Owned Enterprises, Regional-Owned Enterprises, women's organizations, Employment Social Security Administering Body and Health Social Security Administering Body, as well as other agencies that have a role in efforts to implement women's empowerment in the field of employment.

Article 19

The implementation of Women's Empowerment in the field of law as referred to in Article 15 paragraph (2) letter c number 4 is carried out by the work unit in charge of law in the form of:
a. increasing awareness and knowledge in the field of law through communication, information, and education services; and
b. facilitation of access and legal consultation services.

Article 31

In the context of implementing the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government carries out coordination with the central government, provincial government, other regency/city governments, related agencies, law enforcement institutions, service institutions, educational institutions, religious institutions, community social institutions, Islamic boarding schools, professional organizations, legal aid organizations, youth organizations, broadcasting supervisory institutions, media, communities, professional institutions, the business sector and other stakeholders.

2.6.text:
Article 34

1. To ensure synergy, continuity and effectiveness in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women, the Regional Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women in the Region.
3. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted periodically from planning through to policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women for the current year.

Article 35

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women shall be conducted by the Regional Apparatus implementing governmental affairs in the field of women's empowerment on a regular basis.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs and activities for the protection and empowerment of women shall be used as input for the formulation of policies, programs and activities.

Article 35

Paragraph (1)
"Periodically" referred to means the time to conduct monitoring and evaluation at least once every 3 (three) months or at any time if necessary.

Paragraph (2)
Sufficiently clear.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Women are persons of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

3.9.text: Integrated Services are the implementation of integrated, multi-aspect, cross-functional and cross-sectoral services for victims, victim citizens, and/or witnesses of criminal acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination. 26. Complaint is a series of reporting actions carried out by victims and/or companions to the Integrated Service Center organizers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against victims of violence. 27. Health Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims of violence from the health disorders they suffer. 28. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring the psychological condition and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 29. Legal Assistance is legal services provided by companions, law enforcement officers which include providing legal consultation, exercising power, representing, accompanying, defending and taking other legal actions for victims of violence. 30. Repatriation is an effort to return victims of violence from the receiving area/where the violence occurred to the area of origin or family. 31. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims of violence with family, community, institutions or other social environments that can provide protection. 32. Exploitation is an act with or without the victim's consent which includes but is not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or practices similar to slavery, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully moving or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. 33. Discrimination as referred to is any restriction, harassment, or exclusion that is directly or indirectly based on human differentiation on the basis of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, group, class, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs, which results in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life both individually and collectively in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural fields, and other aspects of life. 34. Regional Technical Implementation Unit for the Protection of Women and Children hereinafter abbreviated as UPTD PPA is an operational technical implementation unit in a work unit that administers government affairs in the field of women's empowerment and child protection, which functions as an organizer of integrated services for women and children who experience violence, discrimination, and other problems. 35. Village/Sub-district Women and Children Protection Group hereinafter abbreviated as KPPAD/KPPAK is a community-based women's and children's protection institution that is domiciled and carries out women's and children's protection work in the village/sub-district area according to their place of residence.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Kebumen Regency. 2. Regent is the Regent of Kebumen. 3. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the Regional House of Representatives of Kebumen Regency. 5. Regional Apparatus is an auxiliary element of the Regent and DPRD in government affairs that are the authority of the region. 6. Implementation is the execution of a matter carried out to achieve a goal. 7. Women are persons of female sex starting from infants, adolescents, adults up to the elderly, who have been recognized by law. 8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting and providing a sense of security to women as well as the fulfillment of their rights through consistent, structured, and systematic attention aimed at achieving gender equality. 9. Empowerment of Women is an effort to obtain access and control over resources, economy, politics, social, culture, so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capacity and self-concept. 10. Discrimination against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex, which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status, on the basis of equality between men and women. 11. Gender Equality is an equal condition and position between men and women to obtain their rights as human beings, in accessing and controlling resources, participating in all development processes and decision-making, as well as obtaining benefits from development. 12. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect and hindering the ability to enjoy all rights and freedoms. 13. Violence Against Women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in misery or suffering of women physically, sexually, and psychologically, including threats of certain actions, arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the private or public sphere. 14. Economic Violence is a form of violence in which the perpetrator controls, manipulates, or restricts the victim's access to economic resources with the aim of controlling and dominating the victim, including acts of: taking full control of the victim's income, including salary, savings, or other financial assistance received by the victim, restricting or prohibiting the victim from owning or using money, so that the victim is completely dependent on the perpetrator for financial needs, prohibiting or preventing the victim from working or continuing education with the aim of limiting the victim's financial independence, using the victim's assets or property for personal gain or damaging such assets as a form of punishment, and making all financial decisions without involving the victim, so that the victim has no control over household finances. 15. Physical Violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death. 16. Psychological Violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and/or other psychological suffering to a person. 17. Sexual Violence is any act in the form of rape, indecent acts, forced contraception, forced sterilization, sexual torture, sexual exploitation, sexual slavery, electronic-based sexual violence, acts violating decency that are contrary to the victim's will, forced prostitution, criminal acts of trafficking in persons aimed at sexual exploitation and other forms of sexual violence that are expressly stated as criminal acts of sexual violence as regulated in the provisions of laws and regulations. 18. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband, wife, or husband, wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 19. Household is husband, wife, children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, foster care, and guardianship representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household. 20. Victim is a woman who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence. 21. Women's Rights are a set of rights inherent in a woman or group of people not to experience discrimination, misery or suffering either directly or indirectly committed by state apparatus or by the state or by regional government apparatus or individuals which are natural rights given by God Almighty. 22. Prevention is all efforts to prevent acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women and the recurrence of acts of violence, exploitation and discrimination against victims. 23. Services are all efforts and actions to fulfill the rights of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination against women which include complaint services, health, social rehabilitation, legal assistance and enforcement, repatriation, social reintegration, and restitution. 24. Victim Recovery is all efforts and actions to strengthen the capacity of women victims of violence, exploitation and discrimination physically, psychologically, legally, socially, politically and economically so as to obtain a dignified and prosperous life. 25.

ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF KEBUMEN REGENCY

NUMBER 01 OF 2025 CONCERNING THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROTECTION AND EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.

Pasal 26

Regional Government is responsible for:
a. implementing policies, programs, activities for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in order to realize the fulfillment of women's rights;
b. facilitating facilities and infrastructure for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women; and
c. applying service standards for the implementation of protection and empowerment of women in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

I. GENERAL

Women are an inseparable part of citizens who have human rights that must be protected and fulfilled without exception. However, various problems such as violence, exploitation, and discrimination are still frequently experienced by women in Kebumen Regency. In addition, access to educational services, health, employment, and participation in development is still limited, which causes gender inequality and impacts the low quality of life of women. This Regional Regulation is prepared as a manifestation of the Regional Government's responsibility in providing guarantees for the protection of women's rights and creating a fair, inclusive system that favors vulnerable groups. This Regional Regulation aims to prevent acts of violence, exploitation, and discrimination against women, provide services and recovery for victims, meet the special needs of women, and improve the welfare and quality of life of women comprehensively and sustainably.

It is hoped that through this Regional Regulation it can become a comprehensive legal foundation to strengthen protection efforts and encourage the empowerment of women so that they are able to be empowered and independent in all aspects of life.
